Title: AurkA inhibitors enhance the effects of B-RAF and MEK inhibitors in melanoma treatment.

Journal/Date: Journal of translational medicine (2014)

MeSH Keywords: Aurora Kinase A, Cell Line, Tumor, Cell Proliferation, Humans, Immunohistochemistry, Ki-67 Antigen, Melanoma, Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase Kinases


--- ABSTRACT ---
[BACKGROUND]: Aurora kinase A (AurkA) is over-expressed in melanoma and its inhibition has been observed to limit tumor growth, suggesting a potential role in melanoma treatment.
[METHODS]: A human melanoma cell line with the B-RAF (V600E) mutation (A375mel) was exposed to B-RAF inhibitor (GSK2118436), MEK inhibitor (GSK1120212) and AurkA inhibitor (MLN8054) as single agents or in various combinations (BRAF plus AurkA inhibitor, MEK plus AurkA inhibitor or triple combination BRAF plus MEK plus AurkA inhibitor). Cell proliferation was assessed using xCELLigence technology. Total protein extracts were examined for p53 and c-Myc protein expression by Western blot analysis. Drug anti-tumor effects were further assessed using a 3D-human melanoma skin reconstruction model, in which tissues were incubated with serum-free medium containing control, B-RAF plus MEK inhibitor, MEK plus AurkA inhibitor or the triple combination.
[RESULTS]: AurkA inhibitor plus B-RAF inhibitor, AurkA inhibitor plus MEK inhibitor or triple combination had a markedly greater anti-proliferative effect on A375 (BRAFV600E) melanoma cells than single agents. In the 3D human skin model, the triple combination had a greater anti-tumor effect at the epidermal/dermal junction than control or either double combination. However, S-100 and Ki-67 positively stained spindle-shaped cells were detected in the dermal stratum, suggesting the presence of alive and proliferating melanoma cells.
[CONCLUSIONS]: These findings provide new prospects for melanoma research, including combined B-RAF/AurkA inhibition for B-RAF mutated melanomas and MEK/AurkA inhibitor combination for patients without B-RAF mutations. Moreover, for the first time, we have shown that a B-RAF, MEK and AurkA inhibitor triple drug combination offers increased efficacy against melanoma cell growth and might be considered as a potential treatment strategy for enhancing clinical response in melanoma. However, although this triple drug combination was more effective at the epidermal/dermal junction, the suggested presence of alive and proliferating melanoma cells in the dermal stratum could result in drug resistance and disease recurrence. Molecular characterization of these dermal cells may be critical for the development of novel therapeutic strategies.

key_findings.finding: A 2023 metastatic-melanoma patient-derived xenograft study directly tested selective AURKA inhibition with MEK inhibition: alisertib plus trametinib was highly effective ex vivo and in vivo, outperformed standard-of-care therapy in BRAF-mutant PDXs, and retained activity in targeted-therapy-resistant models. The retrieved abstract describes enhanced efficacy and tumor control but does not provide a formal synergy score.

source_tools.relevance: Direct alisertib + trametinib PDX and resistant-model evidence

key_findings.finding: In BRAF- and NRAS-mutant melanoma cell models, MLN8237 (alisertib) induced a compensatory MAPK-resistance program; combined AURKA/BRAF targeting in BRAF-mutant cells and AURKA/MEK targeting in NRAS-mutant cells overcame that resistance signature and increased antiproliferative and apoptotic effects. This is direct combination evidence, but the abstract does not identify the specific BRAF/MEK drug names or report a formal synergy metric.

source_tools.relevance: Mechanistic/direct combination evidence with alisertib in melanoma models

key_findings.finding: AURKA inhibition is also active against BRAF-inhibitor-resistant melanoma: in A375 cells selected for vemurafenib resistance, an AURKA F31I variant was identified with MAPK reactivation, and AURKA inhibition was reported as effective and specific against the resistant cells. This supports a resistance rationale, but it is not a direct combination experiment with vemurafenib and does not establish combination synergy.

source_tools.relevance: Direct resistance model but not combination study

key_findings.finding: Other selective-AURKA melanoma evidence is mechanistic rather than combination evidence: MLN8054 induced apoptosis in A375 and 526 metastatic melanoma cells, independently of BRAF mutational status; and AURKA expression is associated with MAPK/ERK activation and poor prognosis. These findings support rationale but do not demonstrate enhancement of a named BRAF/MEK inhibitor.

No direct clinical evidence was identified for combining an AURKA-selective inhibitor (alisertib/MLN8237, MLN8054, or another selective AURKA inhibitor) with vemurafenib, dabrafenib, encorafenib, trametinib, cobimetinib, or binimetinib in melanoma. The clinical literature retrieved concerns AURKA inhibitors largely as monotherapy or in non-melanoma settings; therefore clinical benefit, safety, and translational feasibility of these combinations remain unestablished.

source_tools.relevance: Clinical-trial search did not identify a melanoma AURKA + BRAF/MEK combination trial

key_findings.finding: The evidence located is principally selective AURKA-specific, not pan-Aurora: MLN8054 and alisertib/MLN8237 are described as AURKA-directed agents in the direct melanoma studies. No convincing direct melanoma combination study using a pan-Aurora inhibitor with the requested BRAF/MEK inhibitors was identified; pan-Aurora or broader Aurora literature should not be substituted for these AURKA-specific results.
